You are composing music in an isolated workspace. Use the bash tool to run commands and complete the task.
Each command runs in /workspace in a fresh bash shell; files and the FT2 session persist between commands. Budget: no limit on steps, 120 minutes; a step is one reply, and every tool call in it runs in order. Every tool result ends with <time_left>, the minutes remaining.
A command still running after 120 seconds is stopped and returns exit code 124 (137 if it had to be killed). Command output over 20,000 bytes shows only its first and last 10,000 bytes.
The `ft2 list` command describes the tracker tools. `ft2 call TOOL 'JSON_OBJECT'` calls one tool. `ft2 batch FILE.json` executes a list of {"name": TOOL, "arguments": {...}} calls in order.
This FT2 build exposes samples, instruments by name, patterns, order, tempo, save and render. Envelopes and note-to-sample mapping are unavailable; shape sounds in the sample data itself.
Python 3 and NumPy are available for creating original sound material, editing files, and analyzing renders. Writing the XM bytes yourself is allowed. Keep it a real tracker module, with instruments and patterns doing the work, not one long pre-rendered sample.
The workspace is offline: no network, no coding-agent client, no skill library. You cannot hear audio; render to WAV with module_render and inspect the result with NumPy to check your work, then revise.
A keygen tune plays in a loop. Compose so the module loops cleanly from its end back to its restart position.
Save the final editable module as /workspace/submission/tune.xm. A WAV preview and source scripts may accompany it. The submission directory may hold at most 128 MiB in at most 4096 regular files (subdirectories are fine; links and special files are not). If the accompanying files break these limits they are dropped and only tune.xm is kept. A trusted process renders the final XM separately.
If the time budget runs out, the session stops and the tune.xm saved at that moment is collected as the submission.
Submit by running exactly this command:
echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT
Submission ends the session. There is no second attempt or post-submission repair.

You have FastTracker II and Python/NumPy at your disposal. Make an original keygen tune. Music only.
Choose the sound, tempo, harmony, rhythm, instruments, length and arrangement yourself.

summary.text:
I will compose an original keygen tune using FastTracker II.

The plan is a fast, looping chiptune with 8–16 channels. It will use saw and square leads, arpeggios, punchy drums, and FM-style basses in a major key. The tempo will be 125–180 BPM with speed 3–6. I will generate original samples with Python/NumPy, build the instruments, compose the patterns, save as an XM file, render it, and verify a clean loop.

The tune will be called "Neon Cipher." It avoids generic 90s keygen tropes and instead uses a darker, more sophisticated palette. The sound will feature square leads, fast arpeggios, distorted bass, and tight drum patterns.

The title is now "Azure Lattice." It will run at 145 BPM with 8 channels and speed 4. The key is D minor with a Dorian lift.

The track will use 10 channels at 132 BPM with speed 4. It will run 16 to 24 patterns in a tight loop of eight unique arrangements. The structure is an intro, main groove, lead entry, breakdown, full chorus, and a clean return to the main groove. I am designing eleven original samples: kick, snare, hats, bass, lead, arpeggiator, pad, bell, and crash.

Drums will be one-shot samples with no loops. Bass and lead will use attack-plus-looped-sustain shapes, while pads will bake in a slow attack before looping. The key is shifting to A minor or C# minor for a more distinctive feel.

The key is now C# minor. The progression will be i-VI-III-VII: C#m, A, E, B. Tempo is 138 BPM at speed 3 for a busy, punchy feel.

The tempo is now 140 BPM at speed 4. Each pattern will be 64 rows, or four bars. The arrangement will run eight patterns: an intro, a drum-and-bass groove, a full chord section, two lead melodies, a filter breakdown, and a final chorus. The loop will start at pattern 2 to skip the intro.

The arrangement is now 12 order positions with pattern reuse. The loop will start at pattern 1, skipping the intro. The sequence runs: intro, groove A, full chord section, verse lead, answer, breakdown, chorus, second chorus, then back to the chord section and verse.

The ten channels are now mapped to specific roles: kick, snare, hats, bass, arpeggiator, chord pad, lead, lead harmony, FX, and countermelody. I will generate all samples as WAV files using only NumPy to avoid aliasing. The kick will be a 40–80 Hz sine sweep with a sharp click.

The snare will be a 180 Hz damped sine with highpassed noise. The clap is multiple noise bursts. The closed hat is a short highpassed noise. The open hat is longer. The crash is long noise with metal partials. The bass is an additive square or saw with a punchy attack and loop. The lead is a bright 25% pulse with slight vibrato baked in. The arpeggiator is a short plucky square with decay. The pad uses detuned saws with a slow attack and loop. The pluck is karplus-strong or decaying pulse. The tom is a sine sweep. The bell is FM or additive inharmonics.

I am now checking FastTracker II sample flags to configure forward loops and 16-bit depth. Bass and lead samples will be built with an attack portion followed by a clean loop cycle. C-4 will serve as the base pitch for these waveforms. I am ready to generate the samples and assemble the module.

I am now writing the lead melody. A pentatonic C# minor scale is the base, with 16th-note runs and arpeggiated phrases to match the keygen feel.

The lead phrase is now set to four bars of C# minor. It uses 16th-note runs and arpeggiated phrases for an anthemic keygen feel. The bass will anchor the root on beats with driving 8th-note offbeats.

Arpeggios will use tracker 037 and 047 effects on the C#m, A, E, and B chords. The drum pattern places kicks on beats one and three with extra hits on 2.5 and 3.5 for drive. Snares land on beats two and four. Hats play eighth- or sixteenth-note accents with occasional crashes at phrase starts. Volume column commands will create sidechain-like accents and fades.

I will generate all WAV samples with Python first. Then I will create the module and load the samples. Pattern data will be written in one batch JSON file to avoid thousands of individual ft2 calls. I am now refining the kick sound design.

The kick will be about 80 ms long, using a 40 Hz exponential sweep and a 2 kHz click with tanh saturation. The snare body is a 200 Hz decaying tone plus 80 ms noise and a 400 Hz transient. Hats are highpassed white noise at 30 ms for closed and 150 ms for open, mixed with metallic sine partials. The bass will be a 4096-sample attack followed by a 2048-sample loop of integer cycles, played at C-4.

The bass loop period does not divide evenly into 44100 Hz. I will round the waveform to a clean integer cycle length and use XM finetune to correct the pitch.

The lead will be a single bandlimited pulse with a separate channel for detuned harmony. The arpeggiator pluck is a short decaying square without looping. The pad will be a long looped saw with many harmonics at low volume. An FM bell will provide accent sounds. A supersaw-style hoover bass is also planned.

I will generate the samples as WAV files and load them via sample_load rather than using base64 PCM. The kick will sit at volume 64 for punch, while the bass stays mid-range around 80–200 Hz to avoid being too subby on tracker speakers.

I am now writing the high-quality synthesis code. The instrument list has expanded to sixteen samples, adding a sine sub-bass, a clean saw bass, and a rimshot. Panning will be set manually: hats slightly right, the arpeggiator left, the lead center, and chord stabs spread wide across two channels.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Synthesize original tracker samples for Azure Lattice keygen."""
import os
import wave
import numpy as np

SR = 44100
OUT = "/workspace/src/samples"
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

rng = np.random.default_rng(0xA2URE)  # stable seed (hex-like)

def write_wav(name, y, sr=SR):
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=np.float64)
    m = np.max(np.abs(y)) + 1e-12
    y = y / m
    # leave headroom
    y = np.clip(y * 0.95, -1.0, 1.0)
    pcm = (y * 32767.0).astype(np.int16)
    path = os.path.join(OUT, name)
    with wave.open(path, "wb") as w:
        w.setnchannels(1)
        w.setsampwidth(2)
        w.setframerate(sr)
        w.writeframes(pcm.tobytes())
    return path, len(pcm)

def fade(y, nin=32, nout=64):
    y = y.copy()
    n = len(y)
    nin = min(nin, n // 4)
    nout = min(nout, n // 4)
    if nin > 0:
        y[:nin] *= np.linspace(0, 1, nin)
    if nout > 0:
        y[-nout:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, nout)
    return y

def env_exp(t, a, d):
    """fast attack, exponential decay (a, d in 1/seconds-ish)."""
    att = 1.0 - np.exp(-t * a)
    dec = np.exp(-t * d)
    return att * dec

def bandlimited_osc(n, freq, sr, kind="saw", duty=0.25, nyq_frac=0.45):
    t = np.arange(n, dtype=np.float64) / sr
    max_h = max(1, int((sr * nyq_frac) / freq))
    y = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.float64)
    if kind == "saw":
        for h in range(1, max_h + 1):
            y += (1.0 / h) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * h * t)
        y *= 2.0 / np.pi
    elif kind == "square":
        for h in range(1, max_h + 1, 2):
            y += (1.0 / h) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * h * t)
        y *= 4.0 / np.pi
    elif kind == "pulse":
        # Fourier pulse
        for h in range(1, max_h + 1):
            y += (2.0 / (h * np.pi)) * np.sin(h * np.pi * duty) * np.cos(
                2 * np.pi * freq * h * t - h * np.pi * duty
            )
    elif kind == "tri":
        for h in range(1, max_h + 1, 2):
            sign = 1.0 if ((h - 1) // 2) % 2 == 0 else -1.0
            y += sign * (1.0 / (h * h)) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * h * t)
        y *= 8.0 / (np.pi ** 2)
    elif kind == "sine":
        y = np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * t)
    return y

def one_pole_hp(x, cutoff, sr):
    rc = 1.0 / (2 * np.pi * cutoff)
    a = rc / (rc + 1.0 / sr)
    y = np.zeros_like(x)
    prev_x = 0.0
    prev_y = 0.0
    for i, v in enumerate(x):
        ny = a * (prev_y + v - prev_x)
        y[i] = ny
        prev_x, prev_y = v, ny
    return y

def one_pole_lp(x, cutoff, sr):
    rc = 1.0 / (2 * np.pi * cutoff)
    a = (1.0 / sr) / (rc + 1.0 / sr)
    y = np.zeros_like(x)
    prev = 0.0
    for i, v in enumerate(x):
        prev = prev + a * (v - prev)
        y[i] = prev
    return y

def tanh_sat(x, drive=1.5):
    return np.tanh(x * drive)

# ---------------- drums ----------------

def make_kick():
    dur = 0.32
    n = int(SR * dur)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    f0, f1 = 168.0, 46.0
    f = f1 + (f0 - f1) * np.exp(-t * 28.0)
    phase = np.cumsum(2 * np.pi * f / SR)
    body = np.sin(phase)
    body *= np.exp(-t * 9.5)
    # extra sub
    sub = np.sin(np.cumsum(2 * np.pi * (38 + 40 * np.exp(-t * 20)) / SR))
    sub *= np.exp(-t * 7.0) * 0.55
    # beater click
    click = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 2100 * t) * np.exp(-t * 90)
    click += np.sin(2 * np.pi * 4200 * t) * np.exp(-t * 140) * 0.4
    noise = rng.standard_normal(n) * np.exp(-t * 70) * 0.08
    y = body * 0.95 + sub * 0.7 + click * 0.22 + noise
    y = tanh_sat(y, 1.8)
    y = fade(y, 4, 80)
    return y

def make_snare():
    dur = 0.26
    n = int(SR * dur)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    body = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 196 * t) * np.exp(-t * 18)
    body += np.sin(2 * np.pi * 330 * t) * np.exp(-t * 22) * 0.45
    body += np.sin(2 * np.pi * 180 * t) * np.exp(-t * 14) * 0.35
    noise = rng.standard_normal(n)
    noise = one_pole_hp(noise, 1800, SR)
    noise *= np.exp(-t * 14.5)
    snap = rng.standard_normal(n)
    snap = one_pole_hp(snap, 4000, SR) * np.exp(-t * 55)
    y = body * 0.55 + noise * 0.85 + snap * 0.35
    y = tanh_sat(y, 1.3)
    y = fade(y, 8, 60)
    return y

def make_clap():
    dur = 0.28
    n = int(SR * dur)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y = np.zeros(n)
    delays = [0.0, 0.011, 0.019, 0.028, 0.042]
    amps = [1.0, 0.75, 0.55, 0.4, 0.7]
    decays = [90, 80, 70, 60, 12]
    noise = rng.standard_normal(n)
    noise = one_pole_hp(noise, 900, SR)
    for d, a, dec in zip(delays, amps, decays):
        s = int(d * SR)
        env = np.zeros(n)
        tt = np.arange(n - s) / SR
        env[s:] = a * np.exp(-tt * dec)
        y += noise * env
    y = tanh_sat(y, 1.2)
    y = fade(y, 4, 80)
    return y

def make_chh():
    dur = 0.07
    n = int(SR * dur)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y = rng.standard_normal(n)
    # metallic partials
    metals = [4200, 6400, 7800, 9100, 11200, 13500]
    for i, f in enumerate(metals):
        y += 0.15 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * t + i) * np.exp(-t * (40 + i * 8))
    y = one_pole_hp(y, 6000, SR)
    y *= np.exp(-t * 55)
    y = fade(y, 4, 20)
    return y

def make_ohh():
    dur = 0.22
    n = int(SR * dur)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y = rng.standard_normal(n)
    metals = [3800, 5400, 7200, 8800, 10500, 12800]
    for i, f in enumerate(metals):
        y += 0.12 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * t + i * 0.4) * np.exp(-t * (10 + i * 2))
    y = one_pole_hp(y, 4500, SR)
    y *= np.exp(-t * 12)
    y = fade(y, 6, 80)
    return y

def make_crash():
    dur = 1.4
    n = int(SR * dur)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y = rng.standard_normal(n) * 0.5
    partials = [320, 445, 680, 910, 1240, 1680, 2120, 2870, 3560, 4890, 6400, 8200]
    for i, f in enumerate(partials):
        det = 1.0 + 0.003 * np.sin(i)
        y += (0.18 / (1 + i * 0.15)) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * det * t + i)
    y = one_pole_hp(y, 400, SR)
    y *= np.exp(-t * 2.4)
    y = fade(y, 20, 400)
    return tanh_sat(y, 1.1)

def make_tom():
    dur = 0.28
    n = int(SR * dur)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    f = 140 + 80 * np.exp(-t * 18)
    y = np.sin(np.cumsum(2 * np.pi * f / SR))
    y += 0.3 * np.sin(np.cumsum(2 * np.pi * f * 1.5 / SR))
    y *= np.exp(-t * 10)
    y += rng.standard_normal(n) * 0.04 * np.exp(-t * 40)

    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    # minor triad at C4: C E G  (we'll pitch it with notes; actually play as C)
    # richer: detuned saws on C, a fifth, an octave
    freqs = [C4, C4 * 1.498, C4 * 2.0, C4 * 1.25992]  # C G C E-ish? 1.26 ~ E if major... skip
    # just a fat unison + 5th, chord comes from multiple notes
    y = np.zeros(n)
    for f, a in [(C4, 0.7), (C4 * 0.997, 0.5), (C4 * 1.003, 0.5), (C4 * 2, 0.18)]:
        y += a * bandlimited_osc(n, f, SR, "saw")
    y = one_pole_lp(y, 3200, SR)
    y *= (1 - np.exp(-t * 80)) * np.exp(-t * 5.5)
    y = tanh_sat(y, 1.2)
    y = fade(y, 8, 200)
    return y

def make_pad():
    period = int(round(SR / C4))
    cycles = 32
    n_loop = period * cycles
    n_att = int(0.12 * SR)
    n = n_att + n_loop
    freq = SR / period
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y = np.zeros(n)
    # three slightly-not-detuned harmonics (must loop: use exact integer ratios)
    y += 0.55 * bandlimited_osc(n, freq, SR, "saw")
    y += 0.22 * bandlimited_osc(n, freq * 2, SR, "saw")
    y += 0.12 * bandlimited_osc(n, freq, SR, "tri")
    y = one_pole_lp(y, 2200, SR)
    att = np.ones(n)
    att[:n_att] = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, n_att) ** 1.4
    y *= att
    y = fade(y, 0, 0)
    return y, n_att, n_loop

def make_bell():
    dur = 1.1
    n = int(SR * dur)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    f = C4
    # 2-op-ish additive bell
    ratios = [1.0, 2.01, 2.74, 3.76, 5.4, 8.07]
    amps = [1.0, 0.45, 0.35, 0.18, 0.12, 0.07]
    decays = [3.2, 4.5, 6.0, 8.0, 10.0, 14.0]
    y = np.zeros(n)
    for r, a, d in zip(ratios, amps, decays):
        y += a * np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * r * t) * np.exp(-t * d)
    y *= 1 - np.exp(-t * 120)
    y = fade(y, 8, 200)
    return y

def make_pluck():
    # Karplus-Strong
    freq = C4
    period = int(round(SR / freq))
    dur = 0.5
    n = int(SR * dur)
    buf = rng.standard_normal(period)
    buf = np.clip(buf, -1, 1)
    y = np.zeros(n)
    idx = 0
    prev = 0.0
    for i in range(n):
        v = 0.498 * (buf[idx] + prev)
        prev = buf[idx]
        buf[idx] = v
        y[i] = v
        idx = (idx + 1) % period
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y *= (1 - np.exp(-t * 300))
    y = fade(y, 4, 80)
    return y

def make_noise_riser():
    dur = 1.6
    n = int(SR * dur)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y = rng.standard_normal(n)
    # rising LP
    y = one_pole_hp(y, 400, SR)
    y *= t / t[-1]
    y *= 0.5
    y = fade(y, 100, 80)
    return y

summary.text:
Working out the note-off command and volume column settings for the keygen tune.

Mapping XM effect commands for the keygen tune. Effect 0 is arpeggio, 4 is vibrato, and E effects handle extended parameters like glissando and pattern loops.

The key is C# minor. A four-bar repeating chord loop will use C#m, A, E, and B. I will generate the full song as JSON in Python and test vibrato and arpeggio with NumPy.

The chord loop is fixed as C#m, A, E, B. A descending B-A-G# chorus and an ascending A-E-C#m-B lift are planned. Eight patterns are being mapped out: a 64-row intro with pad drones and a bell motif, plus a groove build with kick, snare, hats, bass, and arpeggiated 16th-note leads.

The remaining patterns are now defined. P2 is a full verse with lead melody A and harmony. P3 is a verse variation with lead B and extra plucks. P4 is a filter break with muted kicks, sliding bass, and half-time builds. P5 is the chorus with full drums, a higher lead, wider chords, and bells. P6 adds a counter melody, open hats, and a crash. P7 is a bridge loop-back echoing the intro. The sixteen-pattern sequence is set as 0, 1, 2, 3, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 5, 6, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6.

The full sixteen-pattern sequence runs about 110 seconds, which is too long for a keygen. I will shorten it to ten patterns instead: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 5, 6, 3. This yields roughly 68.5 seconds of music before looping back.

The final arrangement is a ten-pattern loop: intro, groove, verse A, verse B, extra groove, break, chorus A, chorus B, and a second chorus A that loops back to the groove. This runs about 55 seconds.

Twelve channels are now assigned. Kick, snare, hats, bass, sub-bass, arpeggiator, chord pad, main lead, delayed harmony, pluck counter, crash/tom effects, and bell pad each get their own voice.

The bass line is being mapped to a sixteen-row grid. It uses galloping quarter-note C#2 hits with ghosted offbeat eighths, plus octave jumps and a B1 approach note. The arpeggiator pattern is next.

The arpeggiator will play a repeating C#m sequence across the sixteen-row grid. The drum pattern is now set: kick hits on rows 0, 6, 8, and 14 for a driving floor feel; snare on beats two and four; and open hats on offbeats.

The lead melody is being mapped to a four-bar serial pattern across the sixteen-row grid. Each bar uses eighth and sixteenth-note steps to outline the C#m, A, E, and B chords in a memorable hook.

The lead melody is being refined into a more singable, keygen-style form. A repeated X . X X motif rhythm is being applied across the four-bar sequence. Each bar now uses specific note placements to outline the C#m, A, E, and B chords. Fast 16th-note flourishes will be added at the bar ends.

The harmony channel will echo the lead two rows behind at lower volume using instrument 12. Chord stabs will use XM arpeggio 037 for C#m and 047 for the other chords. The arpeggio speed is set to six ticks per note for a fast, chippy effect.

Chord stabs will use the arpeggio effect on every row of each bar to keep the C#m, A, E, and B notes continuously arpeggiated. The pad channel will hold these chord roots as longer notes.

The pad will hold long C#3, A2, E3, and B2 notes on each bar. Bass note-offs are unnecessary because the pattern retriggers on every row. Open hats will use effect EC6 for tight cuts. The Python composer will emit sparse JSON batches of roughly three thousand cells. Vibrato effect 4 with parameter 0x22 or 0x43 will be added to long lead notes.

Volume slides on pads and fine panning on arpeggiators will add movement. Tempo stays constant for a clean loop. The last pattern ends on B major to cadence into the groove's C#m, so any loop point feels natural.

summary.text:
The track centers on low-frequency energy from a kick drum and bass in C#2.

C#2 is 69.3 Hz, two octaves below the sample's original C4 pitch. The kick body peaks at 49 Hz, and the RMS level sits at 0.13 with no clipping.

The track will be titled "Azure Lattice." It evokes a late-90s/early-2000s scene cracktro with a melancholic, crystalline mood. The harmony centers on C# natural minor, using Dorian lifts and harmonic minor cadences.

The melody is being mapped out note-by-note across 32 eighth-note positions for four bars. Two contrasting sections are planned. The first phrase starts with E5 held over two beats, followed by G#5 and C#5.

The verse melody is now fully mapped across four bars. A soaring chorus melody follows with its own eight-bar phrase. Occasional sixteenth-note ornaments will add texture.

The bass line will use a galloping walk with subtle volume changes and a one-octave sub note on the first beat.

A dedicated 16th-note pluck line will carry the main melody. A background arpeggiated chord will layer underneath. The hi-hat pattern uses 16th-note accents every four rows with ghost notes and a volume curve of 24, 8, 14, 8, 20, 8, 14, 8. Open hats will replace closed hats on offbeats two, six, ten, and fourteen.

A snare roll fill with increasing volume and a tom will close the last four rows of some patterns. The full composer script is being drafted now. Drum samples are locked to their natural pitches: kick stays at C-4, hats at C-5 or D-5, and toms remain at C-4.

Tom samples are assigned to A-3, C-4, and E-4 for varied pitch. Effect codes are mapped to specific tracker commands. Note cuts, retriggers, and delays use extended effect 14. Vibrato is set to speed 4 and depth 2. Empty volume columns omit the volume command entirely.

The 64-row intro will unfold in four stages. The first sixteen rows layer a slow pad, a bell, and sparse plucks. Rows sixteen through thirty-one add a quiet arpeggiated chord and a bell motif. Rows thirty-two through forty-seven introduce hi-hat eighth-note fades, ghost bass notes, and a pad at E3. Rows forty-eight through sixty-three bring full hi-hats, a riser on row forty-eight, kick hits on rows fifty-six and sixty, a snare pickup on rows sixty-two and sixty-three, and a crash ready for the next pattern.

The remaining patterns are assigned as follows: P1 is the drum groove with bass, arpeggiated chords, and no lead; P2 adds the lead and harmony to the verse; P3 is the second verse with extra plucks.

P4 is a filter break that strips the kick, porta bass, and snare-only beats before building back. P5 is the full chorus with lead, crash, and extra open hats. P6 is the climax with dual leads, extra bells, and sixteenth-note bass. P7 is a transition ending on B to resolve into P1.

The pattern order runs 0-1-2-3-1-2-3-4-5-6-5-6-7, starting at position one for a ninety-second first playthrough. The composer script will use helper functions.

The lead will echo at an eighth-note delay with volume 22 and opposite panning. The JSON will be generated in chunks of roughly four hundred commands. Pattern lengths are set to sixty-four rows. The tempo is fixed at 145 BPM with speed six, giving each pattern a duration of about 6.6 seconds.

A high chip arpeggiator on the square channel will layer as a keygen-style upper texture. It will be reserved for the chorus to avoid clashing with the pluck arpeggiator used in the verses.

The break pattern will open with a kick every two bars, snare, hats, and long bass notes with vibrato. The second half will build through sixteenth-note fills, a snare roll, a riser, and a final kick.

To prevent clipping once the lead, chords, pad, and crash are added, the master mix is being reduced. Kick drops to sixty, snare to forty-six, bass to fifty, sub to twenty-eight, arpeggiator to twenty-eight, lead to forty-two, harmony to twenty, pad to eighteen, stab to twenty-four, and hats to twenty-two.

The crash volume is set to 28. The pad sample is confirmed at 10700 int16 samples with a loop start of 5292 and length of 5408, totaling 21444 bytes. A grid-based Python composer structure is being drafted.

Twelve channels are now defined as a Python range. Empty patterns will be cleared before writing. Note-off commands use the string "off". Panning automation will be added via effect 8. Seven dramatic moments are planned: the intro bell atmosphere, the drum drop, the lead entry, the break snare roll, the chip arpeggiator explosion, the final high melody, and a short turnaround. The lead line will use tone porta for slurred notes with speed values between 0x20 and 0x50.

The composer script will be saved as `/workspace/src/compose.py`. It will generate roughly 1500 to 2500 cells in batches of two thousand. The `ft2 batch` command will be used for compilation with error checking. All patterns remain at sixty-four rows for simplicity. The bass root note is fixed at C#2.

Bass patterns are now defined as eight-note templates per chord, with each note mapped to a specific octave. The C#m template uses root, fifth, octave, and walk notes across two octaves. Walking transitions will land on rows fourteen and fifteen at the bar end. A sixteen-note arpeggiator template is also being drafted for the C#m harmony.

The arpeggiator will use eighth-note steps in the verses and sixteenth-note steps in the chorus. The intro pad will hold for one bar with a volume slide-down effect at the end. """Compose Azure Lattice — looping C#m keygen XM patterns."""

import os

KICK, SNR, HAT, BASS, SUB, ARP, CHD, LEAD, HARM, PLK, FX, CHIP = range(12)

cells = []

def put(pattern, row, ch, note=None, inst=None, vol=None, fx=None, fp=None):
    a = {"pattern": pattern, "row": int(row), "channel": int(ch)}
    if note is not None:
        a["note"] = note
    if inst is not None:
        a["instrument"] = inst
    if vol is not None:
        a["volume"] = int(vol)
    if fx is not None:
        a["effect"] = int(fx)
    if fp is not None:
        a["effect_param"] = int(fp)
    cells.append({"name": "pattern_set_cell", "arguments": a})

def cut(p, r, ch, ticks=3):
    put(p, r, ch, fx=14, fp=0xC0 | (ticks & 0xF))

         arp8=["A-4","C#4","E4","G#4","A-4","C#5","E4","C#4"],

def drums_groove(p, bar, b, extra=False, openhat=True, clap=True):
    # four-on-the-floor + syncopation
    kicks = [0, 4, 8, 12]

        kicks += [6, 14]
    elif bar % 2 == 1:
        kicks += [6]
    if bar == 3:
        kicks += [14]
    for r in sorted(set(kicks)):
        vol = 64 if r % 4 == 0 else 48
        put(p, b + r, KICK, "C-4", 1, vol)
    # snare 2 and 4
    put(p, b + 4, SNR, "C-4", 2, 50)
    put(p, b + 12, SNR, "C-4", 2, 52)
    if clap:
        put(p, b + 12, SNR, None, None)  # already snare; clap on FX? layer via delay
        put(p, b + 12, FX, "C-4", 3, 28)  # wait FX used for crash — use?

        put(p, b + 0, BASS, fx=4, fp=0x42)  # vibrato later rows

    # sub on downbeats

    else:

            v = vol if i % 2 == 0 else vol - 6
            put(p, b + i * 2, ARP, n, 13, max(8, v))

        a["note"] = note
    if inst is not None:
        a["instrument"] = inst
    if vol is not None:
        a["volume"] = int(vol)
    if fx is not None:
        a["effect"] = int(fx)
    if fp is not None:
        a["effect_param"] = int(fp)
    cells.append({"name": "pattern_set_cell", "arguments": a})

def drums_groove(p, bar, b, extra=False, openhat=True, clap=True):
    # four-on-the-floor + syncopation

        kicks += [6, 14]
    elif bar % 2 == 1:
        kicks += [6]
    if bar == 3:
        kicks += [14]
    for r in sorted(set(kicks)):
        vol = 64 if r % 4 == 0 else 48
        put(p, b + r, KICK, "C-4", 1, vol)

            vol = 22 if r % 4 == 0 else (12 if r % 2 == 0 else 7)

            put(p, b + i * 2, ARP, n, 13, max(8, v))

        (0, "C#5", 36), (8, "G#4", 24), (16, "A-4", 34), (24, "E-4", 22),
        (32, "E-5", 36), (40, "B-4", 24), (48, "D#5", 32), (56, "B-4", 22),
        (60, "G#4", 20),
    ]
    for r, n, v in bells:
        put(p, r, LEAD, n, 16, v)
    # sparse plucks
    for r, n in [(4, "E-4"), (12, "G#4"), (20, "C#4"), (28, "E-4"),
                 (36, "G#4"), (44, "B-4"), (52, "D#4"), (58, "F#4")]:
        put(p, r, PLK, n, 17, 22)
    # quiet arp from bar 2
    for bar in range(1, 4):
        chd = BARS[bar]
        b = bar * 16
        vol = 12 + bar * 6
        for i, n in enumerate(chd["arp8"]):
            put(p, b + i * 2, ARP, n, 13, vol if i % 2 == 0 else vol - 4)
    # chord arp whisper last 2 bars
    for bar in range(2, 4):
        chord_bar(p, bar, bar * 16, BARS[bar], vol=12)
    # hats fade in last 2 bars
    for r in range(32, 64):
        if r % 2 == 0:
            vol = 4 + (r - 32) // 2
            put(p, r, HAT, "F-5", 4, min(20, vol))
    put(p, 50, HAT, "C-5", 5, 16)
    put(p, 58, HAT, "C-5", 5, 20)
    # bass ghosts last bar
    chd = BARS[3]
    put(p, 48, BASS, "B-1", 9, 22)
    put(p, 56, BASS, "B-1", 9, 28)
    put(p, 60, BASS, "F#1", 9, 24)
    put(p, 62, BASS, "G#1", 9, 30)
    # riser
    put(p, 32, FX, "C-4", 18, 22)
    # kick pickup
    put(p, 56, KICK, "C-4", 1, 40)
    put(p, 60, KICK, "C-4", 1, 52)
    put(p, 62, KICK, "C-4", 1, 36)
    put(p, 60, SNR, "C-4", 2, 28)
    put(p, 62, SNR, "C-4", 2, 40)
    put(p, 63, SNR, "C-4", 2, 50)
    # chip sparkle
    put(p, 0, CHD, "C#5", 12, 10, fx=0, fp=0x37)
    for r in range(1, 16):
        put(p, r, CHD, fx=0, fp=0x37)

# ----- P1 GROOVE -----
def build_groove(p=1, with_lead_hint=False):
    put(p, 0, FX, "C-5", 6, 30)  # crash
    for bar in range(4):
        b = bar * 16
        chd = BARS[bar]
        fill = (bar == 3)
        if fill:
            drums_fill(p, b)
        else:
            drums_groove(p, bar, b, extra=(bar == 2), clap=False)
        bass_bar(p, bar, b, chd, driving=True, vol=52)
        arp_bar(p, bar, b, chd, density=8, vol=30)
        chord_bar(p, bar, b, chd, vol=18)
        pad_bar(p, bar, b, chd, vol=18)
        pluck_bar(p, bar, b, chd, vol=24)
        put(p, b + 0, LEAD, chd["bell"], 16, 22)  # soft bells
    # tiny lead hint last 8 rows
    if with_lead_hint:
        put(p, 56, HARM, "E-5", 11, 28)
        put(p, 58, HARM, "G#5", 11, 24)
        put(p, 60, HARM, "C#6", 11, 32)
        put(p, 62, HARM, "B-5", 11, 22)

build_groove(1, with_lead_hint=True)

# ----- P2 VERSE A -----
def build_verse_a(p=2):
    put(p, 0, FX, "C-5", 6, 24)
    for bar in range(4):
        b = bar * 16
        chd = BARS[bar]
        drums_groove(p, bar, b, extra=(bar == 1), clap=False)
        bass_bar(p, bar, b, chd, driving=True, vol=52)
        arp_bar(p, bar, b, chd, density=8, vol=28)
        chord_bar(p, bar, b, chd, vol=16)
        pad_bar(p, bar, b, chd, vol=16)
        pluck_bar(p, bar, b, chd, vol=22)
    ev = lead_verse_a()
    place_lead(p, ev, inst=11, vib_rows=[4, 20, 36, 52])
    echo_lead(p, ev, delay=2, voldiv=2.5, inst=12)

build_verse_a()

# ----- P3 VERSE B -----
def build_verse_b(p=3):
    for bar in range(4):
        b = bar * 16
        chd = BARS[bar]
        if bar == 3:
            drums_fill(p, b)
        else:
            drums_groove(p, bar, b, extra=True, clap=False)
        bass_bar(p, bar, b, chd, driving=True, vol=54)
        arp_bar(p, bar, b, chd, density=16, vol=26, pan_sweep=True)
        chord_bar(p, bar, b, chd, vol=18)
        pad_bar(p, bar, b, chd, vol=16)
    ev = lead_verse_b()
    place_lead(p, ev, inst=11, vib_rows=[8, 20, 38])
    echo_lead(p, ev, delay=2, voldiv=2.6, inst=12)
    # extra high sparkle
    put(p, 36, FX, "E-6", 16, 28)
    put(p, 52, FX, "F#5", 16, 22)

build_verse_b()

# ----- P4 BREAK -----
def build_break(p=4):
    # bars 0-1: sparse
    for bar in range(2):
        b = bar * 16
        chd = BARS[bar]
        put(p, b + 0, KICK, "C-4", 1, 50)
        put(p, b + 4, SNR, "C-4", 2, 36)
        put(p, b + 12, SNR, "C-4", 2, 40)
        put(p, b + 8, KICK, "C-4", 1, 28)
        for r in range(0, 16, 2):
            put(p, b + r, HAT, "F-5", 4, 10 if r % 4 else 16)
        put(p, b + 0, BASS, chd["root2"], 9, 44)
        put(p, b + 8, BASS, chd["fifth2"], 9, 32)
        put(p, b + 0, SUB, chd["root1"], 10, 34)
        arp_bar(p, bar, b, chd, density=8, vol=22)
        chord_bar(p, bar, b, chd, vol=14)
        pad_bar(p, bar, b, chd, vol=20)
        put(p, b + 0, LEAD, chd["bell"], 16, 30)
        put(p, b + 8, PLK, chd["plk"][2], 17, 26)
    # bar 2: rebuild
    bar = 2
    b = 32
    chd = BARS[2]
    for r in (0, 4, 8, 12):
        put(p, b + r, KICK, "C-4", 1, 50)
    put(p, b + 4, SNR, "C-4", 2, 44)
    put(p, b + 12, SNR, "C-4", 2, 48)
    for r in range(16):
        put(p, b + r, HAT, "F-5", 4, 10 + r // 2)
    bass_bar(p, bar, b, chd, driving=True, vol=48)
    arp_bar(p, bar, b, chd, density=16, vol=24)
    chord_bar(p, bar, b, chd, vol=16)
    put(p, 32, FX, "C-4", 18, 26)  # riser
    # bar 3: snare roll into chorus
    drums_fill(p, 48)
    chd = BARS[3]
    bass_bar(p, 3, 48, chd, driving=True, vol=50)
    arp_bar(p, 3, 48, chd, density=16, vol=28)
    chord_bar(p, 3, 48, chd, vol=18)
    # lead climb
    for r, n, v in [(32, "B-4", 28), (36, "E-5", 32), (40, "G#5", 36),
                    (44, "B-5", 40), (48, "C#6", 36), (52, "D#6", 40),
                    (56, "E-6", 46), (60, "F#6", 50), (62, "G#6", 54)]:
        put(p, r, LEAD, n, 11, v)

def build_chorus_a(p=5):
    put(p, 0, FX, "C-5", 6, 34)
    for bar in range(4):

def build_chorus_b(p=6):

summary.text:
The drum chorus has a channel conflict: claps on the PLK channel clash with plucks.

Drums_groove also overwrites the FX channel with claps, stealing crash, tom, and riser sounds. The plan is to apply all batches first, render, then fix issues after listening.

The PLK channel conflict is harmless. The clap on beat 4 sits cleanly between pluck hits.

A partial-update bug remains. The API may overwrite only the effect field while preserving the existing note.

The API replaces unspecified fields with zero. Sending only an effect field wipes the note and instrument from that cell. This breaks layered patches like lead instruments or chord notes.

The partial-update bug is confirmed. Lead vibrato and arp echo/pan patches both wipe their notes. These must be merged into single put calls. Empty chord rows are safe because they intentionally have no note.

The 92-second duration is correct. The earlier 185-second figure was a misread of stereo sample counts.

Sub-bass and kick are muddy. The sub oscillator needs reduction. Midrange instruments need boosting to cut the low-end clutter. A slight DC offset remains. Peak volume is safe. RMS is loud enough.

Lead and chord energy in the 1–4 kHz band is only 4.4%, far too quiet for a keygen. The lead pulse sample must be brighter and louder. Sub volume will drop from 44 to 24, with pattern volumes reduced. Bass will get a stronger highpass, the kick tail cut, and its own volume lowered. The pad may also add low mud. A DC block will be applied.

The lead pulse is too thin and lowpass-filtered at 9000 Hz. It needs a brighter, louder instrument volume. Bass and sub will drop to roughly 40 and 18–24. Lead will rise to 64. The bass lowpass will also fall to reclaim midrange space.

Bass lowpass will be set to roughly 1200 Hz to free up midrange for the lead. Kick volume is fixed at 56. The pad sits at 138 Hz, which is acceptable. The loop cadence from pattern 6 into pattern 1 is musically satisfying. The module will rely on its player to enforce a clean loop.

The crash on pattern 1 row 0 may cause a click at the loop boundary. Hi-hats are too quiet at only 2.7% in the 3–8 kHz band and need boosting. The bass saw currently layers a sub sine at 0.35, which doubles the sub effect; that will be removed. The sub instrument itself will be reduced to volume 20 and restricted to bar downbeats.

A-0 at 27.5 Hz is rumble and will be dropped. The lowest sub notes will shift up to A-1, B-1, C#1, E-1, and B-1. For the A chord, sub will be A-1 instead of A-0 so it no longer duplicates the bass root.

The sub channel will be removed entirely from the pattern sequence to eliminate low-end clutter. The bass sample will use a saw-plus-square blend with an 80 Hz highpass and a 2500 Hz lowpass, no sine sub, and more punch. The lead pulse will gain a second harmonic for brightness. The arpeggiator will get a shorter, brighter, sharper attack. Hi-hats will be louder in the sample set.

The kick will be tightened and its click reduced. A snare delay bug in chorus A needs fixing, along with FX channel conflicts. A clap layer cannot share the snare channel, so it will use ghosted rim or clap hits on off-beat patterns instead. The chorus needs more lift: louder leads, more hi-hats, and a crash. The lead uses long notes in the chorus, which is correct.

Lead sample loop continuity will be checked for discontinuities. The arpeggiator will switch to 16th-note patterns in the groove for a sharper keygen feel. The pad will be quieter to reduce low-end clutter. A sidechain-style ducking effect on the pad during kick hits is also being considered.

A concrete volume map is set: kick 60, snare 50, hats 32/18/10, OHH 32, bass 42, sub 16 on C#1 and E-1 only, arpeggiator 40. The clap will be placed on FX row 12 to avoid stealing the PLK effect from the snare. The intro length of 6.6 seconds is acceptable for a keygen.

Final instrument volumes are set: pad 12, lead 64, echo 24, pluck 32, crash 36, bell 28, and chord arpeggiator 28 in the chorus versus 18 in the verse. The tempo is fixed at 145 BPM with effect speed 6. The lead will be fattened into a pulse-plus-saw hybrid, and a second delayed lead doubling will be added to the chorus for slapback depth. The kick frequency will rise from 46 Hz to 55 Hz to cut sub-rumble. The bass highpass will use a one-pole filter since scipy is unavailable. All samples will be regenerated and the module rebuilt from scratch.

A quick volume tweak is being attempted first to avoid a full pattern rebuild. Sub volume drops to 8, bass to 40, lead to 64, arpeggiator to 50, hats to 40, and kick to 54. summary.text:
The lead.wav file contains a significant DC offset of -0.0525.

Bass and square samples are far too hot, while lead and arp are relatively quiet. Bass at C#2 plays two octaves below pitch, spreading energy into 69Hz harmonics. I will rebuild all tonal samples with DC blocking, consistent RMS levels, and proper loop crossfades.

Bass will use HP and LP filters with lower RMS. Lead gets a brighter, lower-duty pulse for more buzz. Square is being reduced in volume. Drums will be normalized separately. A 32-sample crossfade will blend the loop end into the start.

The crossfade implementation blends the loop tail into the head using a linear fade. Pulse and sawtooth waveforms are not zero-mean, which explains the lead's DC offset; subtracting the mean after generation will fix this. Bass tanh saturation is also adding DC.

I will rewrite gen_samples.py and compose.py with a cleaner structure. The sub-bass will be removed or limited to prevent low-end clutter. Chorus snare delay will be fixed, and the mix will stay mid-focused with more empty space in the intro. Sixteenth-note arpeggios will be made more prominent to give the track its keygen DNA. I am also considering ECx note cuts for tighter chip sounds, E9x retriggers on snare fills, and volume accents. The key and tempo will remain C#m at 145 BPM.

Channel 4 will be dedicated to clap and rim shots, replacing the muddy sub-bass. The full 12-channel map is now fixed: kick, snare, hats, bass, clap, arpeggio, chord chip, lead, harmony echo, pluck, FX, and pad. A two-bar hooky motif in C#m and A will anchor the melody.

The lead melody will use a tight eight-note phrase in C#5, E5, and G#5. A classic 16th-note arpeggio runs through C#5, G#4, E4, and B4. The bassline follows an um-ts-um-ts rhythm with octave jumps between C#2 and C#3. A square-wave arpeggio on the chord channel will provide the signature keygen chip sound.

I will generate the rebuilt samples with vectorized NumPy code instead of Python loops. For DC removal, I will subtract the mean after generation. For highpass filtering, I am considering an offline FFT approach rather than recursive IIR filters.

I will use offline FFT filtering with a Butterworth-like frequency response for the rebuilt samples. The new pipeline is gen_samples2.py and compose2.py. I am adding safeguards to prevent accidental cell overwrites from conflicting instruments on the same channel or row. Clap hits will land on channel 4 at rows 4 and 12, while rim shots will occupy rows 3, 7, and 11.

Panning is being assigned to each instrument: arpeggio left, echo right, hats at 160, chord at 100, pad at 80, pluck at 210, lead at 128, and crash at 90. The sixteen-note arpeggio will use effect 8 to ping-pong between left and right. All rebuilt samples will be normalized to a 0.95 peak target, with bass scaled down to 0.7 after filtering so it no longer dominates the mix.

All rebuilt samples will be normalized to a 0.9 peak, then individually scaled: bass at 0.7, lead at 1.0, square at 0.6, and arpeggio at 0.85. The pad will use a 200 Hz highpass and 2 kHz lowpass with a slow attack. The lead will be a pulse wave at 0.125 duty for extra brightness. A noise-perc tick will add 16th-note groove. The tempo stays at 145 BPM.

The arrangement is being tightened to a 12-position loop. The order will be [0, 1, 2, 3, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 5, 6, 7], with the first play lasting about 79 seconds before looping back to the groove. The turnaround at pattern 7 will remain. The kick will be shortened to 200 ms to prevent overlapping mud. Source scripts will be saved alongside the generated files.

I verified that the rebuilt samples are playing back in 16-bit mode. The bass frequency measured at 49–70 Hz, which matches C#2 correctly. Setting flags=1 does not force 8-bit playback; it only enables looping while preserving the original bit depth.

The bass loop length of 1352 samples is correct for its period. I will keep the forward loop and skip ping-pong. The scale sample is slightly flat at -4.5 cents, so a +6 finetune step will bring it into tune.

The scale sample period is being set to 168 for cleaner powers of two. The lead hook is being arranged with rests and accented notes on specific rows to create a tighter, more rhythmic phrase.

Portamento will glide the lead from G#5 to C#6. The FX channel is being split across the arrangement: crash on row 0, toms on rows 5, 7, and 9, a riser on row 32 of the break, and bells on rows 16, 32, and 48. Channel 11 is reserved for pad and bell conflicts, with pad on 11 and lead on 7 in the intro, verse, and chorus.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Keygen-oriented samples: mid-focused, DC-free, loop-safe."""
import os, wave, struct, math
import numpy as np

SR = 44100
OUT = "/workspace/src/samples"
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)

PERIOD = 168  # ~262.5 Hz, finetune later
C4 = SR / PERIOD

def write_wav(name, y):
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=np.float64)
    y = np.nan_to_num(y, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
    y = y - np.mean(y)
    m = np.max(np.abs(y)) + 1e-12
    y = y / m * 0.92
    pcm = np.clip(y * 32767.0, -32767, 32767).astype(np.int16)
    path = os.path.join(OUT, name)
    with wave.open(path, "wb") as w:
        w.setnchannels(1); w.setsampwidth(2); w.setframerate(SR)
        w.writeframes(pcm.tobytes())
    return path, len(pcm)

def fft_eq(x, sr, hp=None, lp=None):
    n = len(x)
    spec = np.fft.rfft(x)
    f = np.fft.rfftfreq(n, 1.0 / sr)
    h = np.ones_like(spec, dtype=np.float64)
    if hp:
        # 2nd order-ish HP
        h *= (f / hp) ** 2 / (1.0 + (f / hp) ** 2)
    if lp:
        h *= 1.0 / (1.0 + (f / lp) ** 2)
    spec = spec * h
    y = np.fft.irfft(spec, n=n)
    return y

def env_ads(n, sr, a=0.003, d=0.2, s=0.0):
    t = np.arange(n) / sr
    att = np.minimum(t / max(a, 1e-4), 1.0)
    dec = np.exp(-t / max(d, 1e-4))
    # after attack, blend toward sustain
    e = att * (s + (1 - s) * dec)
    return e

def bl_osc(n, freq, sr, kind="saw", duty=0.25):
    t = np.arange(n) / sr
    max_h = max(1, int(0.48 * sr / freq))
    y = np.zeros(n)
    if kind == "saw":
        for h in range(1, max_h + 1):
            y += np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * h * t) / h
        y *= 2 / np.pi
    elif kind == "square":
        for h in range(1, max_h + 1, 2):
            y += np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * h * t) / h
        y *= 4 / np.pi
    elif kind == "pulse":
        for h in range(1, max_h + 1):
            y += (2 / (h * np.pi)) * np.sin(h * np.pi * duty) * np.sin(
                2 * np.pi * freq * h * t
            )
    elif kind == "tri":
        for h in range(1, max_h + 1, 2):
            sign = 1 if ((h - 1) // 2) % 2 == 0 else -1
            y += sign * np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * h * t) / (h * h)
        y *= 8 / np.pi ** 2
    elif kind == "sine":
        y = np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * t)
    return y

def looped(kind, duty=0.25, cycles=16, attack=0.006, extra=None, hp=None, lp=None, drive=1.0):
    n_loop = PERIOD * cycles
    n_att = int(SR * attack)
    n = n_att + n_loop
    y = bl_osc(n, C4, SR, kind, duty=duty)
    if extra == "sawmix":
        y = 0.72 * y + 0.28 * bl_osc(n, C4, SR, "saw")
    elif extra == "oct":
        y = 0.8 * y + 0.2 * bl_osc(n, C4 * 2, SR, kind, duty=duty)
    if drive != 1.0:
        y = np.tanh(y * drive)
    if hp or lp:
        y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=hp, lp=lp)
    y = y - np.mean(y)
    att = np.ones(n)
    if n_att:
        att[:n_att] = np.linspace(0, 1, n_att)
    y *= att
    # tiny xfade at loop boundary
    xf = 24
    a = y[n_att:n_att + xf].copy()
    b = y[-xf:].copy()
    fade = np.linspace(0, 1, xf)
    y[-xf:] = b * (1 - fade) + a * fade
    y[:8] *= np.linspace(0, 1, 8)
    return y, n_att, n_loop

# ----- drums -----
def make_kick():
    n = int(SR * 0.22)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    f = 52 + 110 * np.exp(-t * 42)
    phase = np.cumsum(2 * np.pi * f / SR)
    body = np.sin(phase) * np.exp(-t * 14)
    click = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 2800 * t) * np.exp(-t * 120) * 0.35
    click += np.sin(2 * np.pi * 5200 * t) * np.exp(-t * 180) * 0.15
    noise = fft_eq(rng.standard_normal(n), SR, hp=2500, lp=9000) * np.exp(-t * 80) * 0.08
    y = body + click + noise
    y *= np.linspace(0, 1, 6).tolist() + [1] * (n - 6)
    y[-80:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 80)
    y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=28, lp=6000)
    return y

def make_snare():
    n = int(SR * 0.2)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    body = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 210 * t) * np.exp(-t * 22)
    body += 0.4 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * 340 * t) * np.exp(-t * 26)
    noise = fft_eq(rng.standard_normal(n), SR, hp=1800, lp=12000)
    noise *= np.exp(-t * 16)
    snap = fft_eq(rng.standard_normal(n), SR, hp=5000, lp=14000) * np.exp(-t * 50) * 0.5
    y = 0.4 * body + 0.85 * noise + snap
    y[:4] *= np.linspace(0, 1, 4)
    y[-40:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 40)
    return y

def make_clap():
    n = int(SR * 0.24)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    noise = fft_eq(rng.standard_normal(n), SR, hp=1000, lp=10000)
    y = np.zeros(n)
    for d, a, dec in [(0, 1, 70), (0.012, 0.7, 65), (0.021, 0.5, 55), (0.036, 0.85, 14)]:
        s = int(d * SR)
        env = np.zeros(n)
        env[s:] = a * np.exp(-(t[: n - s]) * dec)
        y += noise * env
    y[-60:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 60)
    return y

def make_chh():
    n = int(SR * 0.055)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y = rng.standard_normal(n)
    for i, f in enumerate([5200, 7400, 9100, 11500, 13800]):
        y += 0.2 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * t) * np.exp(-t * (50 + i * 10))
    y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=7000, lp=16000)
    y *= np.exp(-t * 70)
    y[:3] *= np.linspace(0, 1, 3)
    return y

def make_ohh():
    n = int(SR * 0.18)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y = rng.standard_normal(n)
    for i, f in enumerate([4800, 6700, 8900, 11000, 13200]):
        y += 0.16 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * t) * np.exp(-t * (12 + i * 3))
    y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=5500, lp=16000)
    y *= np.exp(-t * 14)
    y[-50:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 50)
    return y

def make_crash():
    n = int(SR * 1.2)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y = rng.standard_normal(n) * 0.4
    for i, f in enumerate([400, 620, 880, 1190, 1760, 2450, 3200, 4100, 5600, 7400, 9800]):
        y += (0.14 / (1 + 0.12 * i)) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * (1 + 0.002 * i) * t)
    y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=500, lp=14000)
    y *= np.exp(-t * 2.6)
    y[:20] *= np.linspace(0, 1, 20)
    y[-300:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 300)
    return y

def make_tom():
    n = int(SR * 0.22)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    f = 150 + 70 * np.exp(-t * 20)
    y = np.sin(np.cumsum(2 * np.pi * f / SR)) * np.exp(-t * 12)
    y += 0.2 * rng.standard_normal(n) * np.exp(-t * 40)
    y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=60, lp=4000)
    y[-50:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 50)
    return y

def make_rim():
    n = int(SR * 0.07)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 920 * t) * np.exp(-t * 55)
    y += 0.5 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * 1800 * t) * np.exp(-t * 70)
    y += 0.35 * fft_eq(rng.standard_normal(n), SR, hp=3000, lp=12000) * np.exp(-t * 90)
    return y

def make_arp():
    n = int(SR * 0.22)
    y = bl_osc(n, C4, SR, "pulse", duty=0.18)
    y += 0.3 * bl_osc(n, C4 * 2, SR, "square")
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y *= (1 - np.exp(-t * 500)) * np.exp(-t * 16)
    y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=180, lp=12000)
    y[-40:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 40)
    return y

def make_stab():
    n = int(SR * 0.4)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y = 0.6 * bl_osc(n, C4, SR, "saw")
    y += 0.4 * bl_osc(n, C4 * 1.002, SR, "saw")  # won't loop, one-shot
    y += 0.15 * bl_osc(n, C4 * 2, SR, "square")
    y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=200, lp=3500)
    y *= (1 - np.exp(-t * 90)) * np.exp(-t * 7)
    y = np.tanh(y * 1.2)
    y[-80:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 80)
    return y

def make_bell():
    n = int(SR * 0.9)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    f = C4
    y = np.zeros(n)
    for r, a, d in [(1, 1, 3.4), (2.003, 0.4, 5.0), (2.76, 0.32, 6.5),
                    (4.07, 0.16, 8.0), (5.43, 0.1, 11.0)]:
        y += a * np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * r * t) * np.exp(-t * d)
    y *= 1 - np.exp(-t * 150)
    y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=200, lp=8000)
    y[-200:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 200)
    return y

def make_pluck():
    period = PERIOD
    n = int(SR * 0.4)
    buf = rng.standard_normal(period)
    buf -= buf.mean()
    y = np.zeros(n)
    idx = 0
    prev = 0.0
    for i in range(n):
        v = 0.496 * (buf[idx] + prev)
        prev = buf[idx]
        buf[idx] = v
        y[i] = v
        idx = (idx + 1) % period
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y *= 1 - np.exp(-t * 250)
    y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=120, lp=6000)
    y -= y.mean()
    y[-80:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 80)
    return y

def make_riser():
    n = int(SR * 1.5)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y = rng.standard_normal(n)
    # rising band
    y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=400, lp=8000)
    y *= (t / t[-1]) ** 1.2
    y[-100:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 100)
    return y

# generate
write_wav("kick.wav", make_kick())
write_wav("snare.wav", make_snare())
write_wav("clap.wav", make_clap())
write_wav("chh.wav", make_chh())
write_wav("ohh.wav", make_ohh())
write_wav("crash.wav", make_crash())
write_wav("tom.wav", make_tom())
write_wav("rim.wav", make_rim())

y, a, L = looped("saw", extra="sawmix", cycles=8, attack=0.012, hp=90, lp=1600, drive=1.4)
write_wav("bass.wav", y)
print("bass", a, L, len(y))

y, a, L = looped("sine", cycles=8, attack=0.008, hp=40, lp=400)
write_wav("sub.wav", y)
print("sub", a, L, len(y))

y, a, L = looped("pulse", duty=0.125, extra="oct", cycles=16, attack=0.004, hp=120, lp=11000, drive=1.15)
write_wav("lead.wav", y)
print("lead", a, L, len(y))

y, a, L = looped("square", extra="oct", cycles=16, attack=0.003, hp=150, lp=9000, drive=1.05)
write_wav("square.wav", y)
print("square", a, L, len(y))

write_wav("arp.wav", make_arp())
write_wav("stab.wav", make_stab())

y, a, L = looped("saw", extra="sawmix", cycles=32, attack=0.1, hp=220, lp=2400, drive=1.0)
write_wav("pad.wav", y)
print("pad", a, L, len(y))

write_wav("bell.wav", make_bell())
write_wav("pluck.wav", make_pluck())
write_wav("riser.wav", make_riser())
print("done")

        for h in range(1, max_h + 1):
            y += np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * h * t) / h
        y *= 2 / np.pi
    elif kind == "square":
        for h in range(1, max_h + 1, 2):
            y += np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * h * t) / h
        y *= 4 / np.pi
    elif kind == "pulse":
        for h in range(1, max_h + 1):
            y += (2 / (h * np.pi)) * np.sin(h * np.pi * duty) * np.sin(
                2 * np.pi * freq * h * t
            )
    elif kind == "tri":
        for h in range(1, max_h + 1, 2):
            sign = 1 if ((h - 1) // 2) % 2 == 0 else -1
            y += sign * np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * h * t) / (h * h)
        y *= 8 / np.pi ** 2
    elif kind == "sine":
        y = np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * t)
    return y

def looped(kind, duty=0.25, cycles=16, attack=0.006, extra=None, hp=None, lp=None, drive=1.0):
    n_loop = PERIOD * cycles
    n_att = int(SR * attack)
    n = n_att + n_loop
    y = bl_osc(n, C4, SR, kind, duty=duty)
    if extra == "sawmix":
        y = 0.72 * y + 0.28 * bl_osc(n, C4, SR, "saw")
    elif extra == "oct":
        y = 0.8 * y + 0.2 * bl_osc(n, C4 * 2, SR, kind, duty=duty)
    if drive != 1.0:
        y = np.tanh(y * drive)
    if hp or lp:
        y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=hp, lp=lp)
    y = y - np.mean(y)
    att = np.ones(n)
    if n_att:
        att[:n_att] = np.linspace(0, 1, n_att)
    y *= att
    # tiny xfade at loop boundary
    xf = 24
    a = y[n_att:n_att + xf].copy()
    b = y[-xf:].copy()
    fade = np.linspace(0, 1, xf)
    y[-xf:] = b * (1 - fade) + a * fade
    y[:8] *= np.linspace(0, 1, 8)
    return y, n_att, n_loop

# ----- drums -----
def make_kick():
    n = int(SR * 0.22)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    f = 52 + 110 * np.exp(-t * 42)
    phase = np.cumsum(2 * np.pi * f / SR)
    body = np.sin(phase) * np.exp(-t * 14)
    click = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 2800 * t) * np.exp(-t * 120) * 0.35
    click += np.sin(2 * np.pi * 5200 * t) * np.exp(-t * 180) * 0.15
    noise = fft_eq(rng.standard_normal(n), SR, hp=2500, lp=9000) * np.exp(-t * 80) * 0.08
    y = body + click + noise
    y *= np.linspace(0, 1, 6).tolist() + [1] * (n - 6)
    y[-80:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 80)
    y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=28, lp=6000)
    return y

def make_snare():
    n = int(SR * 0.2)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    body = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 210 * t) * np.exp(-t * 22)
    body += 0.4 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * 340 * t) * np.exp(-t * 26)
    noise = fft_eq(rng.standard_normal(n), SR, hp=1800, lp=12000)
    noise *= np.exp(-t * 16)
    snap = fft_eq(rng.standard_normal(n), SR, hp=5000, lp=14000) * np.exp(-t * 50) * 0.5
    y = 0.4 * body + 0.85 * noise + snap
    y[:4] *= np.linspace(0, 1, 4)
    y[-40:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 40)
    return y

def make_clap():
    n = int(SR * 0.24)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    noise = fft_eq(rng.standard_normal(n), SR, hp=1000, lp=10000)
    y = np.zeros(n)
    for d, a, dec in [(0, 1, 70), (0.012, 0.7, 65), (0.021, 0.5, 55), (0.036, 0.85, 14)]:
        s = int(d * SR)
        env = np.zeros(n)
        env[s:] = a * np.exp(-(t[: n - s]) * dec)
        y += noise * env
    y[-60:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 60)
    return y

def make_chh():
    n = int(SR * 0.055)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y = rng.standard_normal(n)
    for i, f in enumerate([5200, 7400, 9100, 11500, 13800]):
        y += 0.2 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * t) * np.exp(-t * (50 + i * 10))
    y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=7000, lp=16000)
    y *= np.exp(-t * 70)
    y[:3] *= np.linspace(0, 1, 3)
    return y

def make_ohh():
    n = int(SR * 0.18)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y = rng.standard_normal(n)
    for i, f in enumerate([4800, 6700, 8900, 11000, 13200]):
        y += 0.16 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * t) * np.exp(-t * (12 + i * 3))
    y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=5500, lp=16000)
    y *= np.exp(-t * 14)
    y[-50:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 50)
    return y

def make_crash():
    n = int(SR * 1.2)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y = rng.standard_normal(n) * 0.4
    for i, f in enumerate([400, 620, 880, 1190, 1760, 2450, 3200, 4100, 5600, 7400, 9800]):
        y += (0.14 / (1 + 0.12 * i)) * np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * (1 + 0.002 * i) * t)
    y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=500, lp=14000)
    y *= np.exp(-t * 2.6)
    y[:20] *= np.linspace(0, 1, 20)
    y[-300:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 300)
    return y

def make_tom():
    n = int(SR * 0.22)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    f = 150 + 70 * np.exp(-t * 20)
    y = np.sin(np.cumsum(2 * np.pi * f / SR)) * np.exp(-t * 12)
    y += 0.2 * rng.standard_normal(n) * np.exp(-t * 40)
    y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=60, lp=4000)
    y[-50:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 50)
    return y

def make_rim():
    n = int(SR * 0.07)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 920 * t) * np.exp(-t * 55)
    y += 0.5 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * 1800 * t) * np.exp(-t * 70)
    y += 0.35 * fft_eq(rng.standard_normal(n), SR, hp=3000, lp=12000) * np.exp(-t * 90)
    return y

def make_arp():
    n = int(SR * 0.22)
    y = bl_osc(n, C4, SR, "pulse", duty=0.18)
    y += 0.3 * bl_osc(n, C4 * 2, SR, "square")
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y *= (1 - np.exp(-t * 500)) * np.exp(-t * 16)
    y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=180, lp=12000)
    y[-40:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 40)
    return y

def make_stab():
    n = int(SR * 0.4)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y = 0.6 * bl_osc(n, C4, SR, "saw")
    y += 0.4 * bl_osc(n, C4 * 1.002, SR, "saw")  # won't loop, one-shot
    y += 0.15 * bl_osc(n, C4 * 2, SR, "square")
    y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=200, lp=3500)
    y *= (1 - np.exp(-t * 90)) * np.exp(-t * 7)
    y = np.tanh(y * 1.2)
    y[-80:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 80)
    return y

def make_bell():
    n = int(SR * 0.9)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    f = C4
    y = np.zeros(n)
    for r, a, d in [(1, 1, 3.4), (2.003, 0.4, 5.0), (2.76, 0.32, 6.5),
                    (4.07, 0.16, 8.0), (5.43, 0.1, 11.0)]:
        y += a * np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * r * t) * np.exp(-t * d)
    y *= 1 - np.exp(-t * 150)
    y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=200, lp=8000)
    y[-200:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 200)
    return y

def make_pluck():
    period = PERIOD
    n = int(SR * 0.4)
    buf = rng.standard_normal(period)
    buf -= buf.mean()
    y = np.zeros(n)
    idx = 0
    prev = 0.0
    for i in range(n):
        v = 0.496 * (buf[idx] + prev)
        prev = buf[idx]
        buf[idx] = v
        y[i] = v
        idx = (idx + 1) % period
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y *= 1 - np.exp(-t * 250)
    y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=120, lp=6000)
    y -= y.mean()
    y[-80:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 80)
    return y

def make_riser():
    n = int(SR * 1.5)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    y = rng.standard_normal(n)
    # rising band
    y = fft_eq(y, SR, hp=400, lp=8000)
    y *= (t / t[-1]) ** 1.2
    y[-100:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, 100)
    return y

# generate

        b = bar*16
        ch = CH[bar]
        st = styles[bar] if isinstance(styles, (list, tuple)) else styles

        bass_bar(p, bar, b, ch, vol=bassvol)
        arp_bar(p, bar, b, ch, dens=dens[bar] if isinstance(dens, (list, tuple)) else dens, vol=arpvol)
        chip_bar(p, bar, b, ch, vol=chipvol)
        pad_bar(p, bar, b, ch, vol=14)
        if st != "fill":

summary.text:
The groove is correct. The quiet intro is intentional for a build-then-verse effect, but it must not exceed the drop volume.

The intro is 0.107 RMS versus the groove at 0.077, so the drop feels like a dip. I will quiet the intro by reducing the overlapping pad and chip arpeggiator, then boost the groove drums, bass, and arpeggiator. The square sample loops at full volume across every bar, while the pad retriggers on each pattern.

The intro chip arpeggiator will be lowered, and the pad note-cut or reduced. In the groove, bass volume rises to 50 and chip volume to 24. The kick and snare stay at 64 and 56. A quiet lead ostinato may be added to fill the empty hook tease.

The lead will be added to the verse, and the chorus will be the biggest section. Global sample volumes are being raised first, then the intro will be quieted specifically. The pad will be cut at the end of the intro so the next pattern does not retrigger it. The chip square arpeggiator is still too piercing.

The square sample will drop to 36 so the chip arpeggiator sits back. The chip pattern volume in the chorus rises to 32. A simple octave-bass-syncopated chip lead will fill the groove. The looping pad drones constantly without decay, which is acceptable at quiet levels. The lead vibrato depth is fine. In XM format, vibrato on a held note stops after one row because the effect cell is overwritten by the next note.

FastTracker II requires effect 400 on every row of a held note to keep vibrato alive. I will insert these continuation rows into the lead placement routine.

The arpeggiator will pan more center. A muted pluck on offbeats will add groove energy. The tempo stays at 145 BPM.

The clap volume will be increased. The arpeggiator pan will shift from 64 to 96. A full rebuild of all patterns is cleaner than patching individual cells. The arrangement follows an 80s pop structure: six bars each for intro, groove, verse A, verse B, break, and turn, followed by alternating choruses.

A signature 16th-note run will be added at the end of chorus A. The dense wall of sound in the chorus is intentional. The bass will use a 1600 Hz low-pass filter to give body at low frequencies.

XM volume columns override sample default volumes. Bass volume will be raised directly in the pattern cells rather than through sample_set.

summary.text:
The intro is dominated by a C#3 pad at 139 Hz.

The pad is a continuous saw drone. Its RMS level is 0.41. The 20 kHz peaks are likely FFT leakage or artifacts from hats and risers.

The volume 10 setting may be misinterpreted as an XM volume column command rather than a linear amplitude value. This would explain why the pad remains loud despite appearing quiet.

The math checks out: volume 10 at pad peak 0.41 yields roughly 0.064 RMS, which is low enough on its own. The perceived loudness comes from the pad being the only sound in the intro, since drums and bass dominate the FFT peaks elsewhere.

The fix is to quiet the intro pad—lower volume, a higher thinner note, or a shorter hold—and use bell and arpeggiator instead.

The intro pad will shift to C#4, A-3, E-4, and B-3 at volume 8 for a lighter, more airy sound. The groove pad will drop from volume 12 to 8 everywhere to reduce bass mud. The 20 kHz peaks are likely high-pass filtered hats leaking into the ultrasonic range.

A 16 kHz low-pass filter will be added to all samples for extra cleanliness.

The groove section is too quiet. The chip arpeggiator and bass harmonics need raising to add mid-range energy without the lead voice.

Bass peak amplitude in the groove is only 0.022, which is weak compared to the intro. Raising the bass or brightening its sample by widening the low-pass from 1600 Hz to 2500 Hz should fix this.

The bass sample will be rebuilt with a 3200 Hz low-pass and 80 Hz high-pass, plus a heavier square-wave mix for a sharper chip sound. A second sub-bass layer was considered but rejected as too busy.

The track is nearly mono at 98% stereo correlation, which suits a tracker tune. The arpeggiator, echo, hats, and lead already provide enough width.
